ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic sentence كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I am a pupil (boy).
   B. My name is Ahmad.
   C. I am a pupil (girl).
   D. How are you? (to a girl)

2. Which Arabic sentence means "What is your name? (to a girl)" (1 mark)
   A. أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ
   B. مَا اسْمُكِ؟
   C. أَنَا تِلْمِيذَةٌ
   D. اسْمِي أَحْمَدُ

3. Which Arabic sentence means "My mother cooks." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا أَبِي
   B. هَذِهِ أُمِّي
   C. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ
   D. أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ

4. What does the Arabic sentence الْقِطَّةُ تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The lamp is above the table.
   B. The book is on the table.
   C. The pen is in the bag.
   D. The cat is under the bed.

5. What does the Arabic sentence الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The cat is under the bed.
   B. The book is on the table.
   C. The pen is in the bag.
   D. The lamp is above the table.

6. What is an inferential question? (1 mark)
   A. A question whose answer is stated in the text
   B. A question whose answer is not stated but can be worked out from clues
   C. A question with no answer
   D. A question about spelling

7. Which Arabic sentence means "I see with my eye." (1 mark)
   A. أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   B. أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي
   C. أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي
   D. أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي

8. How is the Arabic word أُذُنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. shaʿr
   B. lisaan
   C. jism
   D. udhun

9. What does the Arabic word ظَهْرٌ (dhahr) mean? (1 mark)
   A. back
   B. nose
   C. leg
   D. ear

10. Which is a sign of fluent speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking as fast as possible
   B. Whispering
   C. Long stops between words
   D. Clear sounds and a steady pace

11. How is the syllable بُ read? (1 mark)
   A. ba
   B. baa
   C. bu
   D. bi

12. Which mark gives the short vowel 'a'? (1 mark)
   A. fatHa, a small slanted line above the letter
   B. kasra, a small line below the letter
   C. Damma, a small curl above the letter
   D. sukuun, a small circle

13. Which Arabic sentence means "My grandfather is old (big in age)." (1 mark)
   A. جَدِّي كَبِيرٌ
   B. أُخْتِي جَمِيلَةٌ
   C. مَرْحَبًا يَا أَحْمَدُ
   D. أَخِي صَغِيرٌ

14. How is the Arabic word عَمَّةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ʿamma
   B. ibn
   C. ukht
   D. ab

15. How is the Arabic word عَصِيرٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. taʿaam
   B. ʿiid miilaad
   C. ʿasiir
   D. shamʿa

16. What does the Arabic sentence أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Water is useful (good for you).
   B. The fish is delicious.
   C. The juice is cold.
   D. I like food.

17. Which Arabic word means "vegetables"? (1 mark)
   A. لَحْمٌ
   B. حَلِيبٌ
   C. مَوْزٌ
   D. خُضَارٌ

18. How is the Arabic word مُفِيدٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. masaa'u l-khayr
   B. nahr
   C. mufiid
   D. jadiid

19. How is the Arabic word كَتِفٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. katif
   B. sinn
   C. shaʿr
   D. raʾs

20. What does the Arabic sentence لِي عَيْنَانِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My body is strong.
   B. I have two eyes.
   C. I have two hands.
   D. This is my body.

21. How is the Arabic word بِيئَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. bii'a
   B. ghaa'im
   C. shajara
   D. zahra

22. Which Arabic sentence means "And the rain is from the sky." (1 mark)
   A. وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ
   B. الشَّمْسُ فِي السَّمَاءِ
   C. مَا أَجْمَلَ الْبِيئَةَ
   D. رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ

23. What does al-miftaahu fii l-khizaana mean? (1 mark)
   A. The key is in the cupboard.
   B. The pen is in the bag.
   C. The chair is at the door.
   D. The lamp is above the table.

24. How is the Arabic word صَحْنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. kitaab
   B. sahn
   C. hadiiqa
   D. khizaana

25. Which Arabic word means "room"? (1 mark)
   A. نَافِذَةٌ
   B. غُرْفَةٌ
   C. كُوبٌ
   D. قَلَمٌ

26. Which Arabic writing style is used in most printed books and newspapers? (1 mark)
   A. Diwani
   B. Thuluth
   C. Naskh
   D. Kufic

27. What does the Arabic sentence الْأَصْدِقَاءُ يَأْكُلُونَ الْكَعْكَةَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I have a gift.
   B. My mother cooks the food.
   C. The friends eat the cake.
   D. I like the party.

28. What does the Arabic sentence الْمَوْزُ لَذِيذٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I drink tea.
   B. I eat rice.
   C. The banana is delicious.
   D. Above the table there is a balloon.

29. Which sentence says 'I clean my teeth'? (1 mark)
   A. unadhdhifu asnaanii
   B. aghsilu wajhii
   C. raʾsii kabiir
   D. aktubu bi-yadii

30. Which word do you use for 'This is ...' before a feminine word such as shams? (1 mark)
   A. haadhihi
   B. man
   C. haadhaa
   D. ayna

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Translate into English: ar-riihu qawiyya (2 marks)

32. Explain why poems help us when learning a language. (2 marks) (2 marks)

33. Translate into English: nahnu narqusu (2 marks)

34. Give three rules for taking turns in a conversation. (3 marks) (3 marks)

35. Translate into English: ash-shamsu fii s-samaa'i wal-ghaymu fii s-samaa'i. (2 marks) (2 marks)

36. Translate into English: aktubu bi-yadii. asmaʿu bi-udhunii. (2 marks) (2 marks)

37. Explain the three reading strategies: decoding, cues and word spacing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

38. Say what a vocabulary bank is and how you can make one from a poem. (3 marks) (3 marks)

39. Translate into English: ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub (2 marks)

40. Translate into English: al-baytu kabiir (2 marks)

41. Write a three-sentence paragraph about your room in Arabic sounds and give the meaning. (5 marks) (5 marks)

42. Give three ways of taking care of your body. (3 marks) (3 marks)

43. Translate into English: haadhihi ummii (2 marks)

44. Write four foods or drinks in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

45. Translate into English: jaddii kabiir (2 marks)

46. Translate into English: baytii kabiir (2 marks)

47. Translate into English: ukhtii taqraʾu (2 marks)

48. Translate into English: akhii yalʿabu (2 marks)

49. Translate into English: laa talʿab bi-s-sikkiin (2 marks)

50. State the job of each part of a speech: opening, middle and closing. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — How are you? (to a girl)
   كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ (kayfa haaluki?) means: How are you? (to a girl)

2. B — مَا اسْمُكِ؟
   مَا اسْمُكِ؟ (maa ismuki?) means: What is your name? (to a girl)

3. D — أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ
   أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ (ummii tatbukhu) means: My mother cooks.

4. D — The cat is under the bed.
   الْقِطَّةُ تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ (al-qittatu taHta s-sariir) means: The cat is under the bed.

5. B — The book is on the table.
   الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ (al-kitaabu ʿalaa t-taawila) means: The book is on the table.

6. B — A question whose answer is not stated but can be worked out from clues
   For inferential questions you use clues in the text to work out the answer.

7. D — أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي
   أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي (anaa araa biʿaynii) means: I see with my eye.

8. D — udhun
   أُذُنٌ is read udhun and means ear.

9. A — back
   ظَهْرٌ (dhahr) means back.

10. D — Clear sounds and a steady pace
   Fluency means smooth speech with clear sounds, steady pace and good intonation.

11. C — bu
   The mark Damma gives the vowel u, so بُ is bu.

12. A — fatHa, a small slanted line above the letter
   fatHa is the mark for the short vowel a.

13. A — جَدِّي كَبِيرٌ
   جَدِّي كَبِيرٌ (jaddii kabiir) means: My grandfather is old (big in age).

14. A — ʿamma
   عَمَّةٌ is read ʿamma and means father's sister.

15. C — ʿasiir
   عَصِيرٌ is read ʿasiir and means juice.

16. D — I like food.
   أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ (uhibbu T-taʿaam) means: I like food.

17. D — خُضَارٌ
   خُضَارٌ (khudaar) means vegetables.

18. C — mufiid
   مُفِيدٌ is read mufiid and means useful.

19. A — katif
   كَتِفٌ is read katif and means shoulder.

20. B — I have two eyes.
   لِي عَيْنَانِ (lii ʿaynaani) means: I have two eyes.

21. A — bii'a
   بِيئَةٌ is read bii'a and means environment.

22. A — وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ
   وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ (wal-maTaru mina s-samaa'i) means: And the rain is from the sky.

23. A — The key is in the cupboard.
   miftaah is key and khizaana is cupboard.

24. B — sahn
   صَحْنٌ is read sahn and means plate.

25. B — غُرْفَةٌ
   غُرْفَةٌ (ghurfa) means room.

26. C — Naskh
   Naskh is clear and round and is used for most printed books.

27. C — The friends eat the cake.
   الْأَصْدِقَاءُ يَأْكُلُونَ الْكَعْكَةَ (al-asdiqaa'u ya'kuluuna l-kaʿka) means: The friends eat the cake.

28. C — The banana is delicious.
   الْمَوْزُ لَذِيذٌ (al-mawzu ladhiidh) means: The banana is delicious.

29. A — unadhdhifu asnaanii
   unadhdhifu means I clean and asnaanii means my teeth.

30. A — haadhihi
   haadhihi is used with feminine words and haadhaa with masculine words.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: The wind is strong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rhythm and rhyme help us to remember words and to practise pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for memory and 1 mark for pronunciation.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: We dance.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen until the speaker finishes; do not speak at the same time; use polite words to interrupt; give others a chance.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid rule.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun is in the sky and the clouds are in the sky.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each half.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: I write with my hand. I hear with my ear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Decoding: sounding out each letter and mark. Cues: using pictures and the sentence to guess. Word spacing: looking at the spaces to see where words begin and end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each strategy.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: A vocabulary bank keeps new words for later. Pick out the words from the poem and write each with its sound, meaning and a picture on cards.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 2 marks for the method.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: On the table there is a cup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: The house is big.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example: haadhihi ghurfatii. fii l-ghurfati sariir. uhibbu ghurfatii. This is my room. In the room there is a bed. I like my room.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence, 1 mark for a beginning-middle-end order and 1 mark for the meaning.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands and face; clean teeth; eat good food; sleep well; play outdoors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid way.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my mother.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example khubz (bread), aruzz (rice), maa' (water), haliib (milk).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: My grandfather is old (big in age).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: My house is big.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: My sister reads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: My brother plays.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not play with the knife.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Opening: greet and say who you are. Middle: give the information. Closing: thank the audience.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.
